question: Similarity (what's near this, over embeddings) can't be a go-directly-there. Does it happen only inside a tree, through the tree's own index, handing back node row numbers, so that no search is ever used to resolve an id?
why_it_blocks: 4.3.1.5.1.2.1 settles identity (fetch by id is never a search); where similarity lives decides what the embeddings index is
answer: yes, similarity lives inside the tree's own index and can be consolidated out during sleep (which is what happens to us humans). everything about this is based on human congnition. yeah, it's all weights. and the embeddings generator provides a layer you're not being aware of at this level. I said embeddings can be attached to any memory node. we have an embeddings generator device spec'd. it's job is to take a question (one that has or will have a tree associated with it by the end of the action), and any piece of data, and run that thru the graph tree. each weight is a number, and an embedding is just a string of numbers. so let's say we're reading a book on biology. and one of the questions is: what are the design patterns in this? so it puts together an embedding based on this node we're storing and the question, and attaches it to the node. let's say it's about a patten for moving energy. now we can do an embedding search for 'patterns about moving energy' and not just get information about electrical or microwave systems, but also about how biology does it. this mimics the cross domain searches my brain does that seem to be unusual. and are a hallmark of the joe bisop/skippy dynamic. so one of our search modes will be cross domain embeddings searches.
